scenarios.action: Keep screen on for setup, then send /echo P0-01-001 through P0-01-010.
Lock screen for two hours; send five echoes before and five after.
Normal 12-hour soak; send one echo about every 30 minutes.
24-hour acceptance soak; send one echo about every 30 minutes.
Disable Wi-Fi for two minutes, re-enable it, then verify an echo within 120 seconds.
Switch Wi-Fi to mobile data and back if a SIM/data plan is available.
Enable airplane mode for two minutes, disable it, then verify recovery within 120 seconds.
Temporarily use a blocked/invalid model route only if this can be done without exposing the key; restore and test one model message. Echo must remain available.
Block Telegram connectivity or disconnect network, restore, and verify echo recovery within 120 seconds.
Reboot Android once. Termux:Boot must restore the service and echo within 120 seconds after unlock/network availability.
Force-stop/kill Termux once. Record whether Android permits automatic recovery without manually reopening Termux.
Open several memory-heavy apps; do not use synthetic root stress tools.
Start at or below 20% battery while unplugged; stop if the device becomes hot or reaches 10%.
12-hour soak on the intended charger in a ventilated location.
Normal use only; do not intentionally heat the phone. Fail if battery temperature exceeds 45 C.
Send 100 uniquely numbered /echo messages at no more than 1 per second.
Send unique echoes around a brief process restart and inspect duplicate message_id events.
Send a model request, kill only the agent PID while it is processing, then send unique echoes after restart.
While the service runs, invoke run-foreground.sh. It must refuse with exit code 73 and no second poller.
Send 50 numbered echoes and compare accepted message IDs to reply events; zero loss and zero duplicate handling required.
